Type Choose what this block will be: a logic operation, a sensor, a timer and so on. Only researched types are listed.
Careful: changing the type resets the block — side roles, every link and every output. It comes back as good as new, so settle on the type before you run wires to it.
Rename Give the block a name of your own instead of the default one.
The name shows in its title and in the link lists of neighbouring blocks. Once a circuit grows and five identical sensors sit side by side, names like "workshop light" save a lot of squinting.
Add link Output Run a signal wire from this block to another one.
Press the button, click this block's output, then the input you want. Click empty tiles to drop route points so the line goes where it suits you instead of straight across. Right-click steps back, Esc cancels. Click the output this link should start from Click the target block.\nLeft-click an empty cell to add a route point; right-click to remove the last. Click this block's input Delete link Hover over a link line and right-click to delete it Show all RimLogic links
Icon color Change the colour of the icon on this block.
It makes no difference to how the block works — this one is purely for you. Handy when similar blocks stand together: different colours tell you at a glance which part of the circuit is which. Power sides: input/output Set up the block's electrical sides: which one takes power in, which one sends it out, and which is switched off.
These are the sides the block ties into the grid with. Turn off the ones you do not need, so wires stop latching on where they have no business being. Signal sides: input/output Set up the block's logic sides: which one receives a signal, which one sends it out, and which is switched off.
These are the sides that signal links attach to. A side that is off shows no indicator and takes no part in the circuit.
Settings Open this block's settings: trigger conditions, values, check areas and modes — whatever its type has to offer. Reconnect power Choose which power line feeds this block.
Useful when several branches run nearby and it matters which one it draws from — say, to keep a block running off the backup line rather than the main one. Press the button, then click the line you want. There is no reachable power conduit nearby. Settings for the selected block. This block has nothing to configure yet.

Timer settings Repeats the input signal on the output after a delay. Set the delay with the slider. Delay ticks
Memory settings Stores a number from the input and keeps it. Whenever the value changes, it sends a pulse. Default value Stored now: {0} Reset
Math block settings Choose an operation. The first number comes from the left input; the second comes from the right. Calculation Comparison Add: first + second Subtract: first − second Multiply: first × second Integer division: first ÷ second Remainder: first mod second Power: first raised to second Square root (uses one number) Absolute value — the number without its minus sign (uses one number) Absolute difference: |first − second| Percent: first × second ÷ 100 Flip sign (uses one number) Equal: 1 if first = second, otherwise 0 Not equal: 1 if first ≠ second Greater than: 1 if first > second Greater or equal: 1 if first ≥ second Less than: 1 if first < second Less or equal: 1 if first ≤ second Approximately equal: 1 if the difference is no more than 1
Multitool settings Choose an operating mode and its settings. Mode Count items: counts the selected item in the area, both on the ground and in storage Toggle device: turns a nearby device on or off by signal Control doors: opens or closes doors in the area by signal Crop maturity: counts harvest-ready plants in the area Item none selected Choose item Device none selected There are no nearby devices that can be toggled. How to react to the signal On while signal is present Each signal toggles Count pawns: counts pawns in the area by filter (groups or one specific pawn) Storage fullness: checks how full the storage in the area is, in percent Who to count All One pawn no pawn selected Choose pawn Which storage Selected All storage in the operating area is counted. no storage selected Choose storage storage
Electrical sides Assign each side a role: take power (input), send power out (output), or do nothing. Up to {0} inputs and {1} outputs. Left-click sets an input, right-click sets an output, and clicking the same side again disables it. Logic sides Assign each side a role: receive a signal (input), send a signal (output), or do nothing. Up to {0} inputs and {1} outputs. Left-click sets an input, right-click sets an output, and clicking the same side again disables it. Only assigned sides show indicators.
